sentences.en: LISA: OK, Greg, so finally managed to read the article you mentioned - the one about the study on gender in physics.
sentences.zh: LISA: 好的，Greg，我终于读完了你提到的那篇文章——就是关于物理学领域性别问题的那项研究。

sentences.en: GREG: About the study of college students done by Akira Miyake and his team?
sentences.zh: GREG: 是指Akira Miyake及其团队针对大学生开展的那项研究吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I was interested that the researchers were actually a mix of psychologists and physicists.
sentences.zh: 我对研究人员的构成很感兴趣，他们实际上是由心理学家和物理学家共同组成的。

sentences.en: That's an unusual combination.
sentences.zh: 这种组合很不寻常。

sentences.en: LISA: Yeah.
sentences.zh: LISA: 是的。

sentences.en: I got a little confused at first about which students the study was based on.
sentences.zh: 我一开始有点困惑，搞不清这项研究究竟基于哪些学生。

sentences.en: They weren't actually majoring in physics - they were majoring in what's known as the STEM disciplines.
sentences.zh: 这些学生其实并非主修物理学，而是主修所谓的STEM学科。

sentences.en: That's science, technology, engineering and ..
sentences.zh: 即科学、技术、工程以及……

sentences.en: GREG: and math.
sentences.zh: GREG: 和数学。

sentences.en: Yes, but they were all doing physics courses as part of their studies.
sentences.zh: 没错，但他们都在学习过程中修读了物理学课程。

sentences.en: LISA: That's correct.
sentences.zh: LISA: 没错。

sentences.en: So as I understood it, Miyake and co started from the fact that women are underrepresented in introductory physics courses at college, and also that on average, the women who do enrol on these courses perform more poorly than the men.
sentences.zh: 所以据我理解，Miyake及其同事的研究起点是：大学基础物理学课程中女性学生人数严重不足，而且平均而言，选修这些课程的女性学生成绩普遍低于男性。

sentences.en: No one really knows why this is the case.
sentences.zh: 目前尚无人真正了解造成这一现象的原因。

sentences.en: GREG: Yeah.
sentences.zh: GREG: 是啊。

sentences.en: But what the researchers wanted to find out was basically what they could do about the relatively low level of the women's results.
sentences.zh: 但研究人员真正想弄清楚的，归根结底是：如何改善女性学生相对偏低的成绩。

sentences.en: But in order to find a solution they needed to find out more about the nature of the problem.
sentences.zh: 然而，要找到解决方案，他们首先需要更深入地了解问题的本质。

sentences.en: LISA: Right - now let's see if I can remember it was that in the physics class, the female students thought the male students all assumed that women weren't any good at physics ... was that it?
sentences.zh: LISA: 没错——现在让我想想，我记得好像是在物理课堂上，女学生们认为男同学们都默认女生不擅长物理……是这样吗？

sentences.en: And they thought that the men expected them to get poor results in their tests.
sentences.zh: 而且她们觉得男生们预期她们在考试中会考得很差。

sentences.en: Audioscripts
sentences.zh: 听力原文

sentences.en: GREG: That's what the women thought, and that made them nervous, so they did get poor results.
sentences.zh: GREG: 这确实是女学生们的想法，而这种想法让她们感到紧张，结果真的考出了较差的成绩。

sentences.en: But actually they were wrong ...
sentences.zh: 但实际上她们想错了……

sentences.en: No one was making any assumptions about.
sentences.zh: 根本没人对她们做出任何假设。

sentences.en: the female students at all.
sentences.zh: 对女学生压根没有任何先入为主的判断。

sentences.en: LISA: Anyway, what Miyake's team did was quite simple getting the students to do some writing before they went into the physics class.
sentences.zh: LISA: 无论如何，Miyake团队所采取的方法相当简单：让学生们在进入物理课堂前先完成一些写作任务。

sentences.en: What did they call it?
sentences.zh: 他们把这叫什么来着？

sentences.en: GREG: Values-affirmation - they had to write an essay focusing on things that were significant to them, not particularly to do with the subject they were studying, but more general things like music, or people who mattered to them.
sentences.zh: GREG: 价值观肯定法（Values-affirmation）——学生需撰写一篇短文，聚焦于对他们自身而言意义重大的事物；这些事物未必与他们正在学习的学科直接相关，而更多是一些更宽泛的内容，比如音乐，或对他们而言重要的人。

sentences.en: LISA: Right.
sentences.zh: LISA: 没错。

sentences.en: So the idea of doing the writing S that this gets the students thinking in a positive way.
sentences.zh: 因此，安排写作任务的用意在于引导学生进行积极思考。

sentences.en: GREG: And putting these thoughts into words can relax them and help them overcome the psychological factors that lead to poor performance.
sentences.zh: GREG: 而将这些积极想法诉诸文字，有助于缓解他们的紧张情绪，并帮助他们克服导致成绩不佳的心理因素。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But what the researchers in the study hadn't expected was that this one activity raised the women's physics grades from the C to the B range.
sentences.zh: 但研究人员未曾预料到的是，仅凭这一项活动，就使女生们的物理课成绩从C等级提升到了B等级。

sentences.en: LISA: A huge change.
sentences.zh: LISA: 变化巨大。

sentences.en: Pity it wasn't to an A, but still!
sentences.zh: 可惜没能升到A等级，但即便如此也相当不错了！

sentences.en: No, but it does suggest that the women were seriously underperforming beforehand, in comparison with the men.
sentences.zh: 不，但这确实表明，此前女生的表现相比男生而言，存在严重的低估现象。

sentences.en: GREG: Yes.
sentences.zh: GREG: 没错。

sentences.en: Mind you, Miyake's article left out a lot of details.
sentences.zh: 不过话说回来，Miyake的文章遗漏了许多细节。

sentences.en: Like, did the students do the writing just once, or several times?
sentences.zh: 例如，学生只做了一次写作任务，还是做了多次？

sentences.en: And had they been told why they were doing the writing?
sentences.zh: 还有，他们是否被告知了进行写作的真实原因？

sentences.en: That might have affected the results.
sentences.zh: 这些因素可能会影响实验结果。

sentences.en: LISA: You mean, if they know if the researchers thought it might help them to improve, then they'd just try to fulfil that expectation?
sentences.zh: LISA: 你的意思是，如果参与者知道研究人员觉得这项活动可能有助于他们提升，那他们就会刻意去满足这种预期？

sentences.en: GREG: Exactly.
sentences.zh: GREG: 没错。

sentences.en: GREG: So anyway, I thought for our project we could do a similar study, but investigate whether it really was the writing activity that had that result.
sentences.zh: GREG: 所以，我想我们这个项目可以做一个类似的研究，但重点考察真正带来该结果的是否确实是写作活动本身。

sentences.en: LISA: OK.
sentences.zh: LISA: 好的。

sentences.en: So we could ask them to do a writing task about something completely different ...
sentences.zh: 那么我们可以让他们完成一个完全不同的写作任务……

sentences.en: something more factual?
sentences.zh: 比如更偏事实性一点的？

sentences.en: Like a general knowledge topic.
sentences.zh: 例如一个常识类话题。

sentences.en: GREG: Maybe or we could have half the students doing a writing task and half doing something else, like an oral task.
sentences.zh: GREG: 也许可以；或者让一半学生做写作任务，另一半做别的任务，比如口头表达任务。

sentences.en: LISA: Or even, half do the same ting task as in the original research and half do a factual writing task.
sentences.zh: LISA: 甚至可以让一半学生完成原始研究中相同的写作任务，另一半则完成一个事实性写作任务。

sentences.en: Then we'd see if it really is the topic that made the difference, or something else.
sentences.zh: 这样我们就能看出，真正起作用的究竟是写作主题本身，还是其他因素。

sentences.en: GREG: That's it.
sentences.zh: GREG: 没错。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: So at our meeting with the supervisor on Monday we can tell him we've decided on our project.
sentences.zh: 所以，周一和导师开会时，我们就可以告诉他，我们已经确定了项目方案。

sentences.en: We should have our aims ready by then. suppose we need to read the original study - the article's just a summary.
sentences.zh: 到那时，我们应该已准备好研究目标。我想我们得先阅读原始研究——目前这篇文章只是个摘要。

sentences.en: LISA: And there was another article I read, by Smolinsky.
sentences.zh: LISA: 还有我之前读过另一篇文章，作者是斯莫林斯基（Smolinsky）。

sentences.en: It was about her research on how women and men perform in mixed teams in class, compared with single-sex teams and on their own.
sentences.zh: 那篇文章探讨了她在课堂上对女性和男性在混合小组、单性别小组以及独立工作三种情境下表现所开展的研究。

sentences.en: GREG: Let me guess ... the women were better at teamwork.
sentences.zh: GREG: 我猜猜……女性在团队合作方面表现更好？

sentences.en: LISA: That's what expected, but actually the men and the women got the same results.
sentences.zh: LISA: 这正是大家原本的预期，但事实上，男性和女性取得了相同的成绩。

sentences.en: whether they were working in teams or on their own.
sentences.zh: 无论他们是小组合作还是单独完成任务。

sentences.en: But guess it's not that relevant to us.
sentences.zh: 不过，这大概跟我们的研究关系不大。

sentences.en: GREG: What worries me anyway is how we're going to get everything done in the time.
sentences.zh: GREG: 让我担心的是，我们如何才能在规定时间内完成所有工作。

sentences.en: LISA: We'll be OK now we know what we're doing.
sentences.zh: LISA: 现在我们明确了方向，应该没问题。

sentences.en: Though I'm not clear how we assess whether the students in our experiment actually make any progress or not
sentences.zh: 尽管我还不太清楚，该如何评估我们实验中的学生是否真的取得了进步。

sentences.en: GREG: No.
sentences.zh: GREG: 是啊。

sentences.en: We may need some advice on that.
sentences.zh: 这方面我们可能需要一些指导。

sentences.en: The main thing's to make sure we have the right size sample, not too big or too small.
sentences.zh: 最关键的是确保样本量合适，既不能太大，也不能太小。

sentences.en: LISA: That shouldn't be difficult.
sentences.zh: LISA: 这点应该不难。

sentences.en: Right, what do we need to do next?
sentences.zh: 好的，接下来我们该做什么？

sentences.en: We could have a look at the timetable for the science classes ... or perhaps we should just make an appointment to see one of the science professors.
sentences.zh: 我们可以先查看一下科学课的课程表……或者，也许我们该直接预约一位科学教授面谈。

sentences.en: That'd be better.
sentences.zh: 后者更好。

sentences.en: GREG: Great.
sentences.zh: GREG: 太好了。

sentences.en: And we could even get to observe one of the classes.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至还能去旁听一节科学课。

sentences.en: LISA: What for?
sentences.zh: LISA: 为什么？

sentences.en: GREG: Well ...
sentences.zh: GREG: 嗯……

sentences.en: OK maybe let's just go with your idea.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也许我们还是先采纳你的建议。

sentences.en: Right, well ...
sentences.zh: 好的，那么……
